text: The following question stood in the name of  Ms He Ting Ru –   9 To ask the Minister for Social and Family Development (a) whether there are any standard training, support or security measures in place for staff of preschools or childcare service providers regulated by the Early Childhood Development Agency to handle unexpected security incidents; and (b) if so, whether any further updates will be made to these measures.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
text: asked the Minister for Social and Family Development (a) what physical security measures are preschools and childcare centres required to put in place to detect and prevent intrusions by unauthorised persons; (b) whether the Ministry regularly checks that these measures are being implemented across all centres; and (c) whether these measures are sufficient to prevent persons with criminal intent from entering the centres and harming staff and children.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: The safety of children in our preschools is of utmost importance.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Such exercises ensure staff and children are familiar with the processes and are able to respond quickly during a crisis like a fire, terrorist attack or bomb threat.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: It also enables preschools to validate and strengthen their SOPs.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: ECDA also reviews regularly the regulatory requirements for preschools and will update them as necessary.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Preschools are also advised to adopt SGSecure advisories, such as “Run-Hide-Tell” and “Press-Tie-Tell”, which MHA shares with the public and organisations to build vigilance and preparedness against terrorism.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Despite the best efforts by ECDA and our preschools to ensure the safety of children and staff, untoward incidents may still occur.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: So, apart from preventive measures, preschools, parents and the wider community must stay vigilant and be prepared to handle such incidents should they occur.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: More fundamentally, it is important to continue to ensure that our society is safe, for example, by having strict controls over gun ownership and maintaining our zero-tolerance stance towards illicit drugs.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Otherwise, it would not just be security in preschools that we have to worry about, but the security for the whole of society.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: In Singapore, during preschool dismissal times, it is common for a large number of caregivers to be fetching their children at the same time and it is difficult for teachers to identify each and every caregiver, and they are likely to use their own subjective judgement to decide whether to open the door to the centre and release the child to the caregiver.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Can I ask the Minister of State whether all preschools are required by regulation to have their doors locked at all times and unlocked only for authorised persons, whose identity is authenticated by the centre staff, and are they required to maintain a list of pre-designated caregivers who are allowed to fetch the children?

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: If these are not spelt out for the preschool centres, could ECDA assess if these enhanced security measures are necessary to ensure the safety of our very young children?

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: As I had mentioned earlier in my main reply, most preschools use electronic locks at the entrance and visitors as well as people leaving the centre are only allowed to do so when there is a proper check and balance of who these persons are.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Though the Member mentioned that there are large numbers of people gathered, potentially, at dismissal time, actually, not all the children leave the preschool at the same time; we have seen staggered dismissal timings as well.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: I am quite sure that the Member, myself included, have been to these preschools when it is dismissal time and we have seen that, actually, the teacher allows the students to go only after the teacher has taken a look at who is the caregiver who is there to pick up the child.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Most schools also would take note of who the caregiver is who picks up the child and there are also instances where, if the caregiver is not someone that the school recognises, the school then checks in with the family.
